doc.title: Lew Tabackin interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

title: Rejecting pop music at South Philadelphia High
summary: He ignored the pop of his time while classmates included Frankie Avalon and Chubby Checker.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Were you at all effected by the popular music that was going on at that time, or were your listening habits pretty well set?

I missed the pop music period. Like a lot of people that I play with, usually younger people, they all said, most of them started listening to the pop music of their time and some of them even played other instruments like guitars and Fender bass, electric basses © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
or whatever. And they were involved in the pop music of their time. I wasn’t. I totally rejected it. From the age of 15 I didn’t deal with it at all.
Yeah. Because rock, let’s see, mid-50s rock & roll was just kind of percolating and just entering the airways.
Well I had no interest. Well I grew up in South Philadelphia. And at South Philadelphia High School was a hotbed of teenage idols and American Bandstand.
Oh yeah that’s right. Fabian and all those guys.
